'''Tarik Biberović''' (born 28 January 2001)<ref name=fborg/><ref name=fiba/> is a Bosnian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He represents [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]] internationally.

== Early life ==
Biberović was born in 2001 in [[Zenica]], where he started his career in KK Ten Zenica.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zeničanin Tarik Biberović izabran na NBA draftu|url=https://www.zenicablog.com/zenicanin-tarik-biberovic-izabran-na-nba-draftu/|publisher=Zenica Blog|access-date=23 June 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== OKK Spars (2016–2018) ===
At the age of 15, Biberović moved to [[Sarajevo]] to the [[OKK Spars]]. He drew attention especially with his performance in the [[Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] with the Spars team in the 2016–2017 season. Playing four games with Spars in this tournament, Biberović stayed on the court for 32.9 minutes and averaged 17.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 blocks.<ref name=fborg/>

=== Fenerbahçe (2018–2026) ===
His potential earned him attention and he wound up linking up with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]], a club that plays in both the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Basketball Super League]] in Turkey and the [[EuroLeague]]. He did not appear in any domestic games for the club during the 2018–19 campaign due to license rules, but he did make his EuroLeague debut in the match against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] on 8 February 2019, at the age of 18. Not much changed the following year, as he made a few EuroLeague appearances but did not play in any Turkish League games. Also, he played at the Turkish Youth League, a level of competition that can hardly be considered challenging for a prospect of his caliber.<ref name=nba>{{cite web|title=About Tarik Biberovic|url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2021/prospects/tarik-biberovic|publisher=NBA.com|access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref>

During the 2020–21 season, though, Biberović played a regular role in the Basketball Super League, appearing in 35 games and starting 11. He continued playing sparingly in EuroLeague games, but he did score 13 points — then his most in a EuroLeague game — against [[ALBA Berlin]] in December 2020 and, with Fenerbahçe missing several players due to COVID-19, played at least 14 minutes in the club's three EuroLeague playoff games and averaged 7.3 points and 3.7 rebounds.<ref name=nba/>

On 19 October 2023, he scored his career high in [[EuroLeague]] with 17 points (1–2 2FG, 5–8 3FG) and 4 rebounds performance win over 101–86, against [[ASVEL Basket|Asvel]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Biberovic's career-high sparked Fenerbahce's record comeback|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/biberovics-career-high-sparked-fenerbahces-record-comeback/|publisher=EuroLeague Basketball|access-date=19 October 2023}}</ref>

On 25 December 2023, he scored his career high in [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Basketball Super League]] with 29 points (with 7 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal, 34 pir) and 4 rebounds performance win over 98–58, against [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka Lassa]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Darüşşafaka Lassa 56–98 Fenerbahçe Beko|url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2023/12/darussafaka-lassa-56-98-fenerbahce-beko|publisher=Fenerbahçe|access-date=25 December 2023}}</ref>

On 15 October 2024, he was suspended for Round 3 of the 2024–2025 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague Regular Season. He was also fined 5,000 [[euros]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Elijah Bryant and Tarik Biberovic to serve suspensions in Round 3 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1728369/elijah-bryant-and-tarik-biberovic-to-serve-suspensions-in-round-3-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=15 October 2024}}</ref> He got into a scuffle under the basket with [[Elijah Bryant]] with referees having to intervene and break them apart, ultimately resulting in both of them being ejected and both were suspended for one match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biberovic and Bryant suspended after Istanbul derby incident, Efes and Fenerbahce will appeal |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1728095/biberovic-and-bryant-suspended-after-istanbul-derby-incident-anadolu-efes-and-fenerbahce-will-appeal/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=14 October 2024}}</ref>

On 29 April 2025, he helped Fenerbahçe to sweep [[Paris Basketball]] as 3–0 in [[2024–25 EuroLeague#Playoffs|playoffs]] with 21 points (7 in overtime, 8–14 FG), 1 rebound and 3 assists performance in 88–98 away wictory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ait Olduğumuz Yerde, Final-Four'dayız! |url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2025/4/fenerbahce-beko-ust-uste-ikinci-kez-final-four-da |website=www.fenerbahce.org |date=29 April 2025 |language=tr}}</ref>

On 25 May 2025, Biberović helped Fenerbahçe to their second EuroLeague championship in [[Abu Dhabi]]. He helped the team defeat the defending champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the semi-final with 15 points (5–9 FG) and 3 rebounds,<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 May 2025 |title=Fenerbahce downs Panathinaikos 82–76, advances to championship game {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-downs-panathinaikos-82-76-advances-to-championship-game/ |access-date=25 May 2025 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}}</ref> and [[AS Monaco Basket|Monaco]] in the final with 3 points (1–4 FG) and 1 rebound.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 May 2025 |title=Fenerbahce crowned 2025 champion with 70–81 win over Monaco |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-crowned-2025-champion-with-70-81-win-over-monaco/ |access-date=25 May 2025 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 10 July 2025, Biberović signed a new three-year deal with the reigning [[EuroLeague]] champions, despite significant interest from the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] who hold his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] rights.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tarık Biberovic üç yıl daha Fenerbahçe Beko’da|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2025/7/tarik-biberovic-uc-yil-daha-fenerbahce-beko-da|website=Fenerbahçe SK|date=10 July 2025|access-date=29 April 2026|language=tr}}</ref> 

After a successful performance in the [[2025–26 EuroLeague|2025–26 EuroLeague season]], he equaled his career record with 26 points (4–5 2FG, 6–8 3FG) in [[2026 EuroLeague Playoffs#Playoff series|the first playoff game]] against [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]] on 28 April 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tarık Biberovic Çıldırdı; Fenerbahçe Beko, Zalgiris’e Karşı 1–0 Öne Geçti!|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/tr/euroleague-tr/1961519/tarik-biberovic-cildirdi-fenerbahce-beko-zalgirise-karsi-1-0-one-gecti/|website=Eurohoops|date=28 April 2026|access-date=29 April 2026|language=tr}}</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2026–present) ===
In June 2023, Biberović was selected in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies select Gregory “GG” Jackson II and Tarik Biberovic in 2023 NBA draft|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-select-gregory-gg-jackson-ii-and-tarik-biberovic-in-2023-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=23 June 2023|access-date=29 October 2023}}</ref> On 8 July 2026, Biberović's draft rights were traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as part of a six-team trade.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 2026 |title=Mavericks Acquire Santi Aldama, Tarik Biberovic and Marcus Sasser |url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/mavericks-acquire-santi-aldama-tarik-biberovic-and-marcus-sasser |access-date=8 July 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On 10 July, Biberović signed a two-year, $6 million contract with Dallas.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 July 2026 |title=Mavericks Sign Tarik Biberović {{!}} Dallas Mavericks |url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/mavericks-sign-tarik-biberovic |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=[[Mavs|mavs.com]] |language=en}}</ref> Biberović wears number 13, though his favorite number is 33; he chose 13 after Fenerbahçe's equipment manager told him it would suit him and bring him luck when he signed his first professional contract at age 15.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biberovic shared a funny story about number 13: "My favorite number is actually 33" |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/2001978/biberovic-shared-a-funny-story-about-number-13-my-favorite-number-is-actually-33/ |website=Eurohoops |date=27 August 2026 |access-date=3 September 2026}}</ref>

==International==
Biberović competed with [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] at [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship]], averaging 7.1 points, 4.1 rebounds and 0.9 assists. Tarik played his best match against [[Latvia men's national under-17 basketball team|Latvia]] in this tournament and scored 16 points.<ref name=fborg/>

In June 2018, he changed his international allegiance so that he could play for [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tarık Biberovic, Türkiye için oynamayı planlıyor|url=https://www.fanatik.com.tr/basketbol/tarik-biberovic-turkiye-icin-oynamayi-planliyor-1380686|publisher=Fanatik|access-date=11 July 2018}}</ref> On 23 February 2024, he played his international debut with [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]] against [[Italy men's national basketball team|Italy]] in the [[EuroBasket 2025 qualification]] game. He recorded 27 points, 8 rebounds and 4 assists in a 87–80 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fenerbahçeli yıldız Tarık Biberovic milli takımda fark yarattı!|url=https://ajansspor.com/haber/fenerbahceli-yildiz-milli-takimda-fark-yaratti-658177|publisher=Ajansspor|access-date=23 February 2024}}</ref> On 25 February 2024, he scored 11 points (also 4 rebounds and 1 assist) including a game-winning buzzer-beater shot to give Turkey a 76–75 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Son sözü Tarık Biberoviç söyledi: Türkiye, İzlanda'yı mağlup etti|url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/sporskor/son-sozu-tarik-biberovic-soyledi-turkiye-izlandayi-maglup-etti,1YlT-Bcts02Byqv7qbsDjg#|publisher=NtvSpor|access-date=25 February 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He was born in [[Zenica]] to [[Bosniaks|Bosniak]] parents.<ref>{{cite web|title=Biberovic's Aba Liga Profile|url=https://www.aba-liga.com/player/3150/23/1/tarik-biberovic/|publisher=Aba Liga Profile|access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref> His younger brother [[Faruk Biberović]] played for Fenerbahçe Beko youth team [[Fenerbahçe Koleji (basketball team)|Fenerbahçe Koleji Novotel]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Faruk Biberovic's Fenerbahçe Profile|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/branslar/basketbolaltyapi/sporcular/fenerbahce-beko-altyapi/faruk-biberovic-tr|publisher=Fenerbahçe SK | access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref>
